description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. title: Netherlands, Germany – Industry specific software development services – Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program (Dynamic Purchasing System - EU-404)
description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

It is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. The information provided in this SSN is subject to change and does not bind the Government to any future obligations. All submissions become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Any information that a respondent considers proprietary and/or copyright should be clearly marked as such. OVERVIEW Requirement: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information System (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Mission Operations (OSPO) requires an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) including site certification, telemetry downlink data services, and satellite commanding data services. This will satisfy NESDIS current requirements for commercial remote telemetry-only downlink for partner missions, Constellation Observing System for Meteorology Ionosphere and Climate-2 (COSMIC-2), Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite�5 (KOMPSAT-5), and PAZ. The GSaaS contract will provide agility for NESDIS to add or reduce ground station service task orders for future NESDIS or partner missions as they are defined. Under this contract, the contractor is responsible for operating ground status sites that meet strict geographical, technical, and regulatory requirements, including securing necessary radio frequency licenses. The contractor shall provide ancillary engineering support services, such as systems compatibility assessments and proficiency testing, while strictly complying with physical security programs, cybersecurity frameworks like NIST or ISO, and government data rights that restrict the external distribution of sensitive information without explicit permission. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS code is 517810 All Other Telecommunications, and the business size standard is $40 million. Key Criteria: Site Requirement � The Contractor shall propose and operate GSaaS at sites that meet the technical specifications for satellite to ground communications and security, that meet mission geographical requirements, and that have availability to meet the Government�s anticipated tasking schedule. Scheduling Requirement � The Contractor shall accept Government service requests according to the scheduling interface agreements in the task order. Service Requirement � The Contractor shall meet the technical performance standard that 95% of scheduled contacts are attempted, successfully completed, that the Eb/N0 margin is greater than 3 dB, and that data are delivered to the specified NOAA internet point of presence within 60 seconds of the end of the contact. Security Requirement � The Contractor shall provide artifacts that demonstrate that sites and services meet security requirements according to the security frameworks established by the Contractor and approved by the Government. Regulatory Requirement � The Contractor shall be solely responsible for local and OPPA Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) IDIQ Performance Work Statement international regulatory compliance related to occupancy and operation of the service sites and for providing the services from those sites. The contractor shall secure, maintain, and comply with radio frequency licenses for the services provided. Required Response Information: Capable small business vendors are requested to provide the following information in response to this SSN announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity ID (UEI). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (beta.SAM.gov). Business Size in relation to NAICS 541715 and any SBA socio-economic certifications. Demonstrated capabilities in meeting the needs of the Key Criteria listed above. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this SSN, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that does not exceed 5 pages. Response Submission Requirements and Deadline: Responses to this SSN should be submitted via e-mail attachments, received no later than 12:00 PM, ET, 9 September 2026 to: Contracting Officer: Trang Tran at Tran.Tran@noaa.gov; and Contracting Specialist: Markita Simmonds at markita.simmonds@noaa.gov.

title: France – Public relations consultancy services – Mission de conseil et de mise en oeuvre du dialogue citoyen au sein de Sète agglopôle méditerranée
description: Le maître d'ouvrage souhaite disposer d'une assistance générale à la définition et la mise en oeuvre de la concertation avec les habitants du territoire et l'animation du collectif des élus communautaires tout au long de la mandature. L'assistance portera sur la définition des stratégies, des modalités, des moyens des différentes formes de dialogues et d'animation et leurs mises en oeuvre. La première étape de la mission consistera à proposer une vision d'ensemble du déploiement d'une stratégie de concertation/animation des 4 grandes cibles du projet - les élus, l'administration, les citoyens, les acteurs sociaux-économiques. Le prestataire devra expliciter les intentions, les méthodes, les moyens, un agenda sur le moyen terme. Plusieurs outils de concertation seront mobilisables pour déployer la stratégie de concertation : l'enquête audiovisuelle, l'enquête large spectre administrée par les habitants, les réunions publiques, les ateliers techniques, la création et diffusion de contenus sur les réseaux sociaux, la création, animation et diffusion de débats au format plateau TV. Il appartiendra au prestataire de les mobiliser en fonction de la stratégie proposée. L'accord-cadre sera exécuté par l'émission de bons de commande. Les prestations sont réglées par des prix unitaires. Le montant maximum est de 800 000 euro(s) HT pour la durée de l'accord-cadre

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Electronic Fax Solution
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 7571TE-26CSS-1527532 has been issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a firm-fixed-price commercial services purchase order for FedRAMP-Compliant Cloud Electronic Fax Solution Integrated with Microsoft Teams BACKGROUND: The mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. To support this mission, IHS requires a secure, cloud-based electronic fax solution that ensures the protection of Protected Health Information (PHI), enhances clinical and administrative workflows, and integrates seamlessly with enterprise collaboration platforms. PURPOSE: � Provide a FedRAMP Moderate or High authorized cloud electronic fax solution � Ensure full integration with Microsoft Teams (native or API-based) � Maintain HIPAA-compliant transmission and storage of PHI � Ensure Government ownership and portability of all fax DIDs � Enable secure, auditable, and reliable fax communications across IHS � Eliminate on-premises fax infrastructure (cloud-only solution) � Provide high availability and continuity of operations SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, software, licenses, cloud services, and support necessary to deliver a fully managed, cloud-native electronic fax solution. Consistent with the sample fax PWS, the contractor shall provide a secure web-based faxing capability with audit logging, encryption, and technical support. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The anticipated period of performance includes one (1) 12-month base period and four (4) 12-month option periods. The base period is September 30, 2026, through September 29, 2027. Each option period, if exercised, will continue for 12 months following the prior performance period. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Cloud-hosted (FedRAMP-authorized environment) Accessible across all IHS facilities nationwide. SOLICITATION INFORMATION Solicitation Number: 7571TE-26CSS-1527532 Request Type: Request for Quotation (RFQ) Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price Commercial Services Set-Aside: Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) Set-Aside under the Buy Indian Act NAICS Code: 518210: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting, and Related Services Small Business Size Standard: $40 million average annual receipts Product Service Code: DA10 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software as a Service. description: DLA Energy, in conjunction with the United States Army, plans to offer the privatization of the water (NAICS 221310) utility system at U.S. Army Garrison -Hawaii (USAG-HI), Island of Oahu, Hawaii. USAG-HI is considering the potential privatization of the water utility systems serving Schofield Barracks � Main Post, Wheeler Army Airfield, Schofield Barracks � East Range, Pililaau Army Recreation Center, Fort Shafter, Tripler Army Medical Center, Fort DeRussy, Helemano Military Reservation, Kahuku Training Area, Aliamanu Military Reservation, and Makua Valley Training Area. The USAG-HI water utility systems to be privatized under this solicitation may include the housing portions of the water utility systems. Utilities Privatization (UP) is defined as the transfer of ownership and responsibility to a municipal, private, regional, district, or cooperative utility company or other entity, for the operations, maintenance, repair, future upgrades, and future utility systems replacements. The conveyance may consist of all right, title, and interest of the United States in the utility system. UP will be accomplished in accordance with 10 U.S.C. �2688 � Utility Systems: Conveyance Authority. As a result of this solicitation, the Contractor will be selected to assume ownership of the water utility system. The new owner shall operate and maintain the system and provide utility services to the Government. Any resulting contract, if awarded, will require the Contractor to furnish all facilities, labor, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to own, maintain, and operate the utility system. All responsibility for maintaining reliable service, including such items as environmental compliance, maintenance costs, major system renovations, construction, equipment, manpower, and overhead costs shall become the utility system owner�s responsibility. The Contractor shall manage the maintenance, repairs, replacement, etc., of the system to ensure continuous, adequate, and dependable service for each Government or tenant connection within the service area. The Contractor shall be responsible for funding all capital investments required to acquire, maintain, and operate the utility system in a safe, reliable condition and to meet the requirements listed in the contract. Real property interests will be conveyed in the form of a Right to Access or an Easement as a reference to the resultant contract. The utility system will be conveyed via a Bill of Sale after a transition period to be determined by the Contractor. Le détail des missions confiées au titulaire figure au cahier des charges. L'accord-cadre sera exécuté par l'émission de bons de commande lors de la survenance du besoin. Les prestations sont réglées par des prix unitaires

title: Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) - Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description: 20 July 2026 Update 1. CSO procedures have been updated, 20 July 2026. 2. Capability Program Executive, C2 Information Network (CPE C2IN) and Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) will be conducting an Industry Day on a forthcoming Call for Solutions (CFS) for NGC2 Scalable Software Applications on Thursday, 23 July 2026 11:00 AM EST. Link to join event: https://usg01.safelinks.protection.office365.us/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdod.teams.microsoft.us%2Fl%2Fmeetup-join%2F19%253adod%253ameeting_673603dad2ac405f8468ad9d5ccb6250%2540thread.v2%2F0%3Fcontext%3D%257b%2522Tid%2522%253a%2522fae6d70f-954b-4811-92b6-0530d6f84c43%2522%252c%2522Oid%2522%253a%2522a4e25b63-4741-4856-a1da-622a11a49d14%2522%252c%2522IsBroadcastMeeting%2522%253atrue%257d&data=05%7C02%7Cglen.r.gearhart2.civ%40army.mil%7C4165c88311c3437c39f508dee653c8e2%7Cfae6d70f954b481192b60530d6f84c43%7C0%7C0%7C639201444683482737%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=jZSFMiuuaD32bMiAguWv6CZDGMTQ6dz%2F8%2F3LO9zc4Ls%3D&reserved=0 3. ACC C2 mailbox has been added for engagements with industry. For escalation / issues please contact Eric.J.Roberts48.civ@army.mil. _________________________________________ Command and Control (C2) is foundational to warfighting, and lessons learned from recent support to contingency operations in Ukraine and Israel, as well as threat assessments in the INDOPACOM AoR, show that the Army�s current C2 information systems should be modernized to meet commanders� needs for large scale combat operations against near peer adversaries. Current mission command systems are not mobile, intuitive, or survivable enough to easily overcome the current threat, changes in the character of warfare, and the pace of technology. As part of the Army�s continuous transformation effort, initiatives are being implemented to transform how the Army operates, trains, and equips for C2 capabilities that enhance its lethality, mobility, and survivability in large-scale combat as part of the Joint Force. The Army�s operational imperative is to improve systems responsibly, using innovative solutions from units and industry; at the same time, preparing for the future by ensuring the next generation of C2 systems are built on a portfolio of capabilities that effectively address emerging threats and ensure dominance over adversaries. The Army�s Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) portfolio of capabilities will provide commanders with the ability to make more, better, and faster decisions through advanced analytics, an integrated data layer, open architecture, and robust and resilient transport. The result is data-centric C2 at every echelon that can operate in any environment. NGC2 requirements are currently being informed by persistent experimentation. Market research and prototyping will create a competitive environment for innovative industry partnerships and continuous integration of new technologies. Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications and Network (PEO C3N) and the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) program is publishing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), W15P7T-25-S-0001, in accordance with the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Subpart 212.70 for the purpose of establishing a streamlined vehicle to award innovative C2 capability and functionality. This CSO will remain open until 16 May 2027. This CSO will be open until canceled by the U.S. Army. Proposals shall only be submitted in response to a Request for White Paper (RWP). *********************************************** *Please note: Supplementary documents pertaining to NGC2 is located on the Joint Communications Marketplace (JCM) at https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/login/, go to �More Communities,� click �Army,� and then �Next Gen Command & Control (NGC2).� The Reading Room is accessed by a link on the NGC2 home page menu. If you have not registered for JCM, please use the following link <https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/register>. If you have registered for JCM, but need access specifically to NGC2 Community page, you must register for access to this space. Please use the following link and register specifically for NGC2 Community Page https://jtnc.experience.crmforce.mil/JTNC/s/register . You will need a Joint Certification Program (JCP) number and Data Custodian to enter the NGC2 community and view CUI documents. If you do not already have a JCP Certification number, please follow the direction below. To gain access to CUI documents, your company/entity must be certified by the Joint Certification Program (JCP). Your entity/company�s Data Custodian requester (designated) on block 3A of the DD Form 2345 is the only authorized individual that can download the controlled attachment. Your entity/company is responsible for the protection of the controlled document after the download. If your entity/company is not pre-certified by the JCP, you will need to apply for certification by completing a DD Form 2345 and emailing it to jcp-admin@dla.mil. Detailed information regarding the JCP application procedures is available at the JCP website at https://www.dla.mil/Logistics-Operations/Services/JCP/. description: Voor het project Verbinding Vierverlaten-Ens 380 kV (VVL-ENS380) moet er onderzoek worden uitgevoerd naar de effectiviteit van Hawk Eye (nieuwe vorm van draadmarkering, zie deze link naar artikel op TenneT website ) en actualisatie van kengetallen naar draadslachtoffers per soort. Beide zijn nodig voor de vergunningverlening voor het project, maar moeten ook TenneT-breed kunnen worden toegepast voor andere lijnenprojecten. Voor de bepaling van het aantal draadslachtoffers onder hoogspanningsverbindingen wordt momenteel gebruikgemaakt van onderzoeksgegevens uit 1987. Deze gegevens sluiten niet langer aan bij de huidige situatie en bieden onvoldoende basis om de ecologische impact van hoogspanningsinfrastructuur zorgvuldig te onderbouwen. Hierdoor ontstaat onzekerheid over de omvang van de effecten op vogelpopulaties en over de effectiviteit van eventuele mitigerende maatregelen. Het beoogde onderzoek kent daarom twee samenhangende doelstellingen. Allereerst wordt een actuele nulmeting uitgevoerd om inzicht te verkrijgen in het aantal draadslachtoffers onder en in de directe omgeving van de bestaande 220 kV-hoogspanningsverbinding tussen Vierverlaten en Ens. Vervolgens wordt de effectiviteit van mitigerende maatregelen onderzocht door deze op geselecteerde masten en geleiders toe te passen en de resultaten te monitoren. Een belangrijk onderdeel van het onderzoek betreft de beoordeling van de effectiviteit van verschillende typen vogelmarkeringen. Binnen de organisatie bestaat een voorkeur voor toepassing van de Hawk Eye-draadmarkering als mitigerende maatregel. Voor een bredere implementatie ontbreekt momenteel echter nog de wetenschappelijke onderbouwing van de effectiviteit ervan onder Nederlandse omstandigheden. Het onderzoek dient daarom de kennisbasis te leveren die nodig is om onderbouwde keuzes te maken over de inzet van deze maatregel en om de bijdrage ervan aan het verminderen van draadslachtoffers aantoonbaar te maken.

Le premier marché a permis d'établir la charte graphique commune à tous les synoptiques, et de réaliser les premiers synoptiques. title: Norway – Software supply services – Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.
description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Deze raamovereenkomst zal worden aangegaan voor een periode van 2 jaar. De ingangsdatum van deze raamovereenkomst is 1 februari 2027. The agreement has a fixed initial duration of six (6) years starting 1 January 2027, with five (5) optional one‑year extensions, for a maximum total duration of eleven (11) years.

title: Netherlands – Articulated trucks – Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem CLAS - Matlogco - Witte Vloot
description: Bedrijfsprofiel De Aanbestedende dienst is het Materieellogistiek Commando Land (MatlogCo) van de Koninklijke Landmacht - een van de zeven onderdelen van het Ministerie van Defensie. Het MatlogCo is verantwoordelijk voor de instandhouding van het grondgebonden materieel van Defensie. Voor meer informatie over het Ministerie van Defensie en het MatlogCo is de website www.defensie.nl te raadplegen. Dynamisch aankoopsysteem De hierbij gebruikte procedure is het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem uit de Aanbestedingswet 2012. De procedure verloopt volledig elektronisch via het online aanbestedingsplatform Negometrix. Een Dynamisch aankoopsysteem (DAS) is een elektronisch proces voor het doen van gangbare aankopen van werken, leveringen of diensten, waarvan de kenmerken wegens de algemene beschikbaarheid op de markt voldoen aan onze behoeften. Doelstelling DAS De doelstelling van het DAS is een zo groot mogelijke groep kwalitatief goede ondernemingen toe te laten zonder de beheersbaarheid te verliezen. Op deze manier creëert Defensie een optimale marktwerking, waarbij Defensie kwalitatief optimale Producten kan selecteren tegen zo laag mogelijke kosten, binnen de gewenste levertijden. Het MatlogCo beoogt hiermee op een eerlijke wijze, snel en eenvoudig haar behoeften op te vullen, door middel van volledige concurrentiestelling. Werking van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem in het kort Voor deze aanbesteding volgt Defensie de Europese aanbestedingsprocedure 'Dynamisch aankoopsysteem', conform de Aanbestedingswet. Hierbij wordt onderscheid gemaakt naar twee fasen: 1. Instellingsfase 2. Gunningsfase Deze fasen worden nader uitgewerkt in vragenlijst 1.1. Kort samengevat Gegadigde dient een Verzoek tot toelating in; Als Gegadigde aan de gestelde eisen voldoet en er geen uitsluitingsgronden van toepassing zijn, wordt zij als Deelnemer toegelaten. Toelating tot het DAS houdt geen opdracht in; Het MatlogCo plaats een nadere uitvraag; Deelnemer schrijft in; Het MatlogCo beoordeelt de Inschrijvingen en gunt aan de economisch meest voordelige Inschrijving. Looptijd van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem Bij de publicatie in maart 2023 had het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS) een initiële looptijd van 48 maanden. Echter, aangezien deze DAS een voortzetting is van de vorige DAS met het negometrix nummer 210681, resteert er nu nog een looptijd van 35 maanden. Het is belangrijk op te merken dat de Aanbestedende Dienst de looptijd één keer kan verlengen, met een periode van 48 maanden. Het staat de Aanbestedende dienst vrij om aan het DAS gedurende de looptijd producten en/of kwalificaties toe te voegen of te verwijderen. Dit zal de Aanbestedende dienst waar nodig aankondigen met een rectificatie.

title: 69--CH-53E Containerized Flight Training Device (CFTD) Baseline Configuration Upgrade (BCU) Pre-Solicitation Teleconference
description: NAWCTSD will host a Pre-solicitation Teleconference (mini-Industry Day) for the CH-53E Baseline Configuration Upgrade (BCU) focused exclusively on the Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard. This standard is referenced for the development of software as a part of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. The pre-solicitation teleconference will take place on Thursday, 06 April 2017 from 1:00 - 3:00 pm EDT. The pre-solicitation teleconference will include a dedicated question and answer period allowing contractors to ask any questions related to the FACE portion of solicitation N61340-17-R-0035. Answers to the questions generated from this pre-solicitation teleconference will be provided to all potential offerors. However, it should be noted that, all questions to the stated solicitation, unrelated to FACE, shall continue to follow normal protocol, with contractors submitting a completed L-1 Question and Answer Form and emailing it to Nicole Knight at Nicole.knight@navy.mil. All interested TSC III Lot II vendors are welcome to call in to this teleconference and should request the dial-in number from NAWCTSD Contracts, Nicole Knight (nicole.knight@navy.mil) no later than 2:30 pm EDT on Wednesday, 05 April 2017. In this request, include your company name, attendees’ names, email addresses, phone numbers, and company address to confirm attendance. Subcontractor requests must be requested through the Prime Contractor. All attendees’ for each company are encouraged to use only one call-in line. The Future Airborne Capability Environment (FACE) Technical Standard is the open avionics standard for making military computing operations more robust, interoperable, portable and secure. The standard enables developers to create and deploy a wide catalog of applications for use across the entire spectrum of military aviation systems through a common operating environment, resulting in lower implementation costs, standards that support a robust architecture and enable quality software development, more capabilities reaching the warfighter faster, and innovation and competition within the avionics industry. FACE is maintained by The Open Group FACE Consortium, a government and industry partnership to define an open avionics environment for all military airborne platform types. The FACE Consortium is a vendor-neutral forum that provides standardized approaches for using open standards with avionics systems. The FACE Consortium works to develop and consolidate FACE open standards, best practices, guidance documents and business models. The Government has included a brief entitled “FACE 101�? for interested contractors to review prior to the teleconference. A NAVAIR Subject Matter Expert (SME) will present this briefing and attendees are encouraged to download the briefing so that they can follow along as he presents the materials. For more information regarding FACE, including the FACE Standards, FACE Data Architecture, The Open Group Architecture Framework Technical Reference Model, and related documentation, please visit the Open Group website at: http://www.opengroup.org/face. Failure of an offeror to call-in to the conference or to submit any questions will be construed to mean that the offeror fully understands all requirements of the solicitation. Prospective offerors are advised that the teleconference will be held solely for the purpose of explaining the FACE Technical Standard as it relates to this solicitation. description: The Department of Justice Canada (JUS) has a requirement for a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform and associated services (via the issuance of Task Authorizations) to support case management of files enabling robust reporting and data analysis. title: Integrated Commercial Vetting and Data-Analysis Pilot Services for USCIS
description: The purpose of this Amendment 0001 is to extend the deadline for responses to this combined synopsis/solicitation to 10 AM ET Wednesday, September 9, 2026 and provide clarification to this combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.202(b)(1). i. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO 12. This announcement (under original posting from August 27, 2026, in conjunction with this Amendment 0001) constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70SBUR26R00000015 is issued as a request for proposal (RFP) for Integrated Commercial Vetting and Data-Analysis Pilot Services. This acquisition is not set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. ii. A list of line-item number(s) and items, quantities, and units of measure. Contract Line-Item Number (CLIN): 0001 Description: Integrated Commercial Vetting and Data-Analysis Pilot Services Quantity: One (1) Unit Identifier: Lot (LO) Period of Performance: September 15, 2026, to October 14, 2026 (Anticipated) Place of Performance: Contractor Owned Facility Product Service Code: B506 � Data Analysis (Other Than Scientific) iii. Description of requirements for the items to be acquired, including documentation supporting any brand name descriptions (see 12.102). USCIS requires timely, scalable, and intelligence-driven capabilities to support the identification of potential fraud indicators and enhanced vetting activities involving individuals throughout the USCIS immigration lifecycle. The required capability must support batch processing of Government-provided target records; identity resolution and corroboration using authoritative commercial and publicly available information; identification and correlation of publicly available online identities and digital activity associated with target records; application of USCIS-designated review criteria; and source documentation sufficient for analyst validation and Government review. The requirement also includes qualified analyst and data scientist support to validate results, reduce duplicative or irrelevant information, refine workflows, and assess pilot performance. Contractor-provided information will support Government analysis and will not constitute an adjudicative, eligibility, enforcement, or adverse-action determination. iv. Date(s) and place(s) of delivery and acceptance and f.o.b. point (see part 47). Period of Performance: September 15, 2026 to October 14, 2026 (Anticipated). Place of performance: Contractor Owned Facility. v. A list of solicitation provisions that apply to the acquisition (see 12.205(a)). See attached Amendment 0001 document(s). vi. A list of contract clauses that apply to the acquisition (see 12.205(b)). See attached Amendment 0001 document(s). vii. The date, time, and place for receipt of offer and point of contact. This posting shall close at 10:00 AM ET on Thursday, September 9, 2026. Contracting Officer: Rachel Turner, rachel.m.turner@uscis.dhs.gov; Contract Specialist: Yamitza Ortiz: Yamitza.m.ortiz@uscis.dhs.gov viii. Any other additional information required by 5.101(c). In accordance with FAR 5.101(c)(4)(vii), based on the market research conducted, the Government intends to award this requirement on a noncompetitive basis to Thomson Reuters Special Services, LLC (TRSS). Market research identified commercial sources capable of providing individual or partial capabilities; however, the Government did not identify another source that demonstrated the ability to provide the complete integrated USCIS requirement within the required 30-calendar-day pilot period. TRSS�s integrated use of CLEAR� Risk Inform/CLEAR Batch with RTIA, Fivecast MATRIX, and specialized analyst/data-scientist support was identified as meeting the Government�s minimum functional requirements. Accordingly, TRSS is the only source identified through market research as capable of satisfying the complete requirement as currently defined. title: Chalk Rock Link Trail Project
description: This solicitation is restricted to Small Business. Project Description: The contractor will be required to clear and grub a trail corridor that is a minimum of 72-inches wide and 80-inches high within the designated path alignment. This work consists of clearing, grubbing, trimming, removing, and treating trees, logs, limbs, branches, brush, plants, and other vegetation within the clearing limits. Clearing practices must include removal down to ground level of any cedar tree that will be trimmed 25% or more. Furthermore, the contractor shall work to avoid any damage to existing, native Burr Oak trees. Cleared vegetation must be removed and piled near the staging area adjacent to the asphalt road for future USACE removal. The trail link will be approximately 2,250 linear feet of bench excavation and tread shaping to establish a stable tread base which follows the alignment in attached Drawing 1, which will be staked by USACE prior to mobilization. The finished trail tread width will range between 36 - 48-inches depending on location and terrain and will be topped with a 4-inch lift of mechanically compacted crushed gravel. The crushed gravel will be placed, graded, and mechanically compacted. Due to the terrain, the final path at minimum will consist of switchbacks with turning platforms to ensure a proper turn radii for both foot and bicycle traffic. The required grade average for the trail tread is 6-8% sustained with a max of 10-15% for no more than 30-foot intervals. Grade reversals and drainage features are required to be installed as preventative measures to promote long-term sustainability. At the halfway point of the trail link, a 4-foot by 8-foot gravel pad with a 4-inch mechanically compacted lift will be constructed adjacent to the trail path for future USACE placement of a cedar log bench. Ground disturbance outside of the clearing limits must be prevented. Significant ground disturbance outside of these limits will result in the contractor's need to perform remedial vegetation measures, as directed by USACE. Site Visit: A site visit is scheduled on August 24th at 10am local time. Contractors will meet at the Natural Resource and Outside Maintenance Facility and then travel to the work site. title: FCI EL RENO FY 27 1ST QTR EGGS
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution, El Reno, Oklahoma, intends to issue solicitation 15B50726Q00000032, for the requirement of QUARTERLY SUBSISTENCE - EGGS. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through FAC 2020-07. The NAICS code for this requirement is 311999, which contains a size standard of number of employees not to exceed 500 employees for small business concerns. Offers will be FOB destination with delivery being specified as 13 weekly Tuesday egg deliveries beginning OCTOBER 06, 2026, and ending DECEMBER 29, 2026. Deliveries will be made to Federal Correctional Institution, 4205 Highway 66 West, El Reno, OK 73036, in accordance with the delivery schedule contained in the solicitation. The contract type will be firm-fixed price. The Government will award to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer conforms to the solicitation based on price. Payments will be made via Government Purchase Card for awards at or below $15,000.00. Awards that are over $15,000.00 will be written as purchase orders and payable by EFT. Invoice(s) are to be sent to the address listed on block 18a of the SF-1449, attention to: FCI El Reno Business Office. The solicitation will be made available on or about AUGUST 26, 2026, and will be posted to the General Services Administration website www.beta.sam.gov. Hard copies of this solicitation will not be made available. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed solely through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The anticipated date for receipt of quotes is SEPTEMBER 09 , 2026. Faith-based organizations and Community-based organizations have the right to submit offers equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered. Point of contact for all information regarding this acquisition is Nate Long, Supervisory Contract Specialist, at the address listed below. Completed offers should be emailed to Nate Long at n2long@bop.gov. The anticipated date of award is SEPTEMBER 10, 2026.

We recently made changes to the Challenge Stream; we have outlined the new parameters: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/challenges Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-uncrewed-ground-system-surveillance-and-reconnaissance?auHash=l-oHqeoTmQmnsxQEUYMY5EaGpYMsj3ef1DLDTsG-TTY MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Ground System for Surveillance and Reconnaissance The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed ground system (UGS) to conduct ground surveillance and reconnaissance (S&R) that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Ground System for Surveillance and Reconnaissance Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 13, 2026 Closing date: September 10, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The Canadian Army (CA) soldier is facing an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the proliferation of multi-spectral sensors and precision weapons that will limit the CA’s ability to conduct surveillance and reconnaissance (S&R) operations and strike enemy targets at range by using attributable ballistic trajectory weapons without the risk of being targeted and attacked. The CA presently lacks an uncrewed ground system (UGS) capable of conducting ground-based surveillance and reconnaissance. The CA requires an innovative UGS that provides an uncrewed alternative to conduct persistent surveillance and route, area, and point reconnaissance tasks. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable, providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be composed of a : a. Ground Vehicle: The vehicle containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor Payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground Control Station (GCS): The system used by the human operator to control the vehicle and manage missions. Example of GCS components includes without limitation, laptop, tablet, handheld controller, etc. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UGS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/ data. e. Battery with Charger: A battery for the UGS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in a temperature range of -20°C and +40°C. 3. Weigh no more than 410kg in an unladen state. 4. Have a minimum operational radius of 3km (unladen) from the GCS while maintaining user control and live video via Radio Frequency link. 5. Operate at a minimum speed of 15km/hr and have a minimum endurance of 4hrs in continuous motion while in an unladen state. 6. Be capable of navigating paved roads, sand trails, and gravel trails during both day and night at a minimum gradient of 15 degrees (approach and lateral). 7. Have front-facing and rear-facing sensors that enable the operator to recognize¹ a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day – Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night – Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 0.5km 8. Be able to look over a minimum 1m obstacle and employ a pan or swivel capability to achieve a minimum of 180-degree field of vision. 9. Have sustained mobility of =7 km/h across while carrying its rated payload across roads, trails, and cross-country terrain. The vehicle must ascend 20% grades, traverse 15% side slopes, negotiate a 250 mm vertical step, and cross a 500 mm trench” ¹. “Recognize” is defined by the Johnson Criteria: Detection, Recognition, and Identification (DRI) are all guidelines that have been set in place by The Night Vision Thermal Imaging Systems Performance Model, also referred to as the Johnson criteria. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%27s_criteria Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to a ready state in 30 minutes or less. This includes completing all tasks (i.e. unstrapping/unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set) such that the vehicle is fully prepped and ready to leave the line of departure. 2. Be sized such that a minimum of 2 UGS can be stowed for transport on a standard palletized loading system (PLS) deck (8 feet wide by 20 feet long). 3. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means that enables the operator to be a minimum of 100m away from the vehicle. 4. Be powered by electric or hybrid engines. 5. Incorporate front automated obstacle avoidance features. 6. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the vehicle. 7. Be transportable by a palletized loading system (PLS). 8. Be recoverable by a NATO-standard tow hook. 9. Have a minimum endurance of 48hrs while stationary and using its sensor payload. 10. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $150,000 CAD or less per system. 11. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UGS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: i. Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); ii. Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); iii. Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; iv. Real-time full motion video feed; and v. Battery life. e. Is capable of interfacing with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UGS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. f. Is able

This project will eliminate identified deficiencies; extend the economic life of the facility by 25 years. Building components and systems to be repaired include the roofing, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC); electrical distribution; water distribution and fire alarm and suppression systems, ceilings, windows, doors, floor coverings, interior reconfiguration, and interior and exterior finishes. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a Full and Open procurement. A small business sub-contracting plan will be required prior to award. SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offeror's proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Potential offerors are invited to submit their past performance, technical, and capability information as described in Section 00 22 16 and Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. As described in Section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, the selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors as Past Performance (for both the Prime Contractor and A/E Designer of Record) and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be requested to submit additional information as described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II are subject to change with the Phase II amendment.) All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. title: Video Game Purchase Plan
description: Description: The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Library Program requires Video Game collection development point system that allow Dept of the Air Force Libraries Division to meet their video game demand. Product characteristics or an equal item must meet to be considered: 1. Must be able to provide materials for collection development in formats that include video games 2. Must be able to provide material of new releases, current best sellers as well as a back catalog of older material 3. Must be able to have 63 libraries individual order accounts under a main account for VCL to manage points 4. Must mail video games up to 63 libraries around the world, shipping costs included in quote 5. Must be able to offer ordering through an online ordering system for 63 libraries 6. Must be able to dedicate customer service representative to resolve all service issues 7. Must be able to provide video games in the following formats: Xbox 1 & X, Playstation 4/5, & Nintendo Switch 8. Must provide a pre-release list to plan upcoming months boxes mut be available on commercial website available for all video game buyers 9. Must provide a suggested monthly order list to DAF libraries. This would be a prefilled cart of newly released suggested titles in DAF Libraries account. 10. Shall provide a commercially available website with an existing multi-tier web-based purchasing system for review and selection of available video games. The system shall offer access to information about publications such as reviews, selection lists, release dates, publisher's list prices, video game covers, descriptions, etc. 11. DAF Libraries does NOT need/want a custom site. We are looking for a video game wholesaler in the library or video game marketplace. 12. DAF 63 Libraries shall have their own unique logins to select items, build carts, and submit selections. 13. Items received in error or in unacceptable condition shall be replaced and shipped to the customer at no additional cost. Return of such items shall not be required. The return window will be more than 30 days due to delays in receiving due to shipping locations. 14. Firm-Fixed Price Order with shipping costs included 15. Shipping shall be via U.S. Postal Service First Class and Priority Mail or similar to APO addresses, either New York, NY or San Francisco, CA. No international shipping is required. 16. No technical or physical processing is required 17. The vendor shall ship items in complete set of 6 games per 20 locations on a monthly basis. Kits must be packaged and labeled separately for each location. 18. Must be able to dedicate a customer service representative to resolve all service issues. 19. DAF Libraries must be able to test the website to evaluate if it meets requirements. Must provide a username and password to see available video games/inventory

title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. This SIR is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.

title: Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry Art in Architecture
description: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the modernization of the Land Port of Entry located in Highgate Springs, VT. GSA is designing and constructing a new facility capable of handling the increased traffic at the port which is located across the U.S.-Canada border from St. Armand, Quebec and adjacent to Lake Champlain. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $400,000 to $500,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by 5:00 PM Eastern Time, September 10, 2026. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry in Highgate Springs, Vermont, must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 5:00 PM Eastern Time, September 10, 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order 13934, Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes, GSA will prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded.

title: IFPC/M-SHORAD Instructional Facility
description: The U.S. Army requires a new instructional facility at Fort Sill to serve as a cornerstone for the modernization and enhancement of its air defense capabilities. Its core mission is to provide soldiers with the critical skills and doctrinal knowledge necessary to operate and maintain two of the Army's newest and most advanced air defense weapon systems: the Indirect Fire Protection Capability (IFPC) and the Maneuver-Short Range Air Defense (M-SHORAD). This facility represents a vital investment in the readiness and lethality of the force, directly supporting the strategic initiative to field one Divisional Air Defense Battalion per Division. It will provide a state-of-the-art environment for hands-on, realistic training that transforms recruits into proficient operators and maintainers. The soldiers trained here will depart Fort Sill prepared to deploy globally, equipped with the skills to ensure the Army's dominance of the airspace and the protection of its ground forces and assets against modern aerial threats. In alignment with Department of War acquisition reform initiatives, the Government is actively leveraging modernized authorities that expand our capability to select alternate, highly collaborative project delivery methods and utilize non-traditional contracting vehicles beyond standard FAR-based constraints. We are seeking critical industry feedback to determine the optimal delivery method (such as Progressive Design-Build, Design-Build to Budget, or Construction Manager at Risk) and procurement pathway to accelerate construction, optimize lifecycle costs, and field this mission-critical capability rapidly. Interested firms are requested to complete the attached market research questionnaire and return it directly to Shay Hill at julie.s.hill@usace.army.mil and Daniel Foyil at daniel.a.foyil@usace.army.mil. Update: 11 AUG 2026 - The Market Intelligence Survey has been updated and is now available in a fillable PDF form. Update: 3 SEP 2026 - Since the initial notice, technical requirements for the IFPC/M-SHORAD General Instructional Facility have progressed to approximately 35% design completion - establishing firmer baselines for site layout, spatial geometry, and core building systems. Because this milestone significantly alters the baseline of project risk and definition, we are expanding our market intelligence to gain a better understanding of how this increased design maturity influences our industry partners' perspective on alternative delivery strategies�specifically Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) and Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk). In addition to the market intelligence survey, Tulsa District is seeking industry's insight and response to the following three questions: Question 1: Re-evaluating Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) at 35% Design Maturity Given that the project has reached 35% design completion, which provides a more defined basis for spatial layout, site geometry, and major building systems, does your firm now consider Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) a more viable delivery method? Specifically, is this level of definition sufficient for your team to competitively propose innovative scope and quality solutions that meet the Government's fixed budget? What key undefined elements (e.g., final simulator utility demands, SCIF accreditation details) would still present significant risk, and how would an OTA framework help mitigate them? Question 2: Re-evaluating Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk) with a Mature Design The initial survey raised concerns about the Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk) model, particularly regarding the prime contractor's inability to self-perform critical trades. With a 35% design now available, if the Government were to retain the Designer of Record but engage a CM under an OTA, how would this change your firm�s interest? What is your primary concern: (a) assuming liability for a design you did not create, or (b) the contractual separation that limits your ability to control project execution through self-performance and direct subcontractor management? Question 3: Identifying the Tipping Point for Price Certainty You previously indicated a design completion of approximately 65% would be needed to provide a reliable Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). With a 35% design package as the starting point, what are the top 2-3 specific technical deliverables (e.g., fully specified long-lead electrical gear, signed-off user requirements for all simulator bays, final force protection and AT/FP requirements) that would allow your team to close the gap from 35% to a firm GMP in the most efficient manner? Would a two-step OTA process, where the selected firm first validates the 35% design and then advances it to GMP, be your preferred approach?

description: Amendment No. 3 (dated 8/26/26) provides responses to vendor questions. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Amendment No. 2 (dated 8/25/26) provides responses to vendor questions and extends the Offer Due Date from 9/8/26 to 9/11/26. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), the Management and Operating (M&O) contractor for Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), intends to construct a new entrance portal at the Laboratory's primary entrance. The existing Main Gate security access point (Building 680), constructed in 1960, has exceeded its useful service life and requires replacement. The project will replace the existing entrance and provide a modernized entrance portal featuring fully integrated security booths to monitor, screen, and process personnel and vehicular traffic entering the Laboratory. The new portal will provide weather protection for security personnel, enhanced site lighting, and a modern traffic control system designed to improve safety, efficiency, and operational reliability. The upgraded entrance will also complement the adjacent, publicly accessible Science and User Support Center (SUSC) by providing a secure, efficient, and welcoming point of entry to the Laboratory. The scope of work for the contract includes the demolition and removal of the existing security booths and associated infrastructure, and the construction of a new entrance portal facility, including structural systems, utilities, security systems, site improvements, and all supporting infrastructure required for full operational capability. BSA will furnish two (2) prefabricated security booths as Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Solicitation documents are available at the link provided in this notice. Mandatory Solicitation Overview Meeting and Site Visit An in-person Solicitation Overview Meeting and Site Visit are MANDATORY for all prospective offerors. Failure to attend both the Solicitation Overview Meeting and the Site Visit will render an offeror ineligible for award under this solicitation. The RSVP must include each attendee's full name and citizenship status. Failure to provide the required information will prevent attendee registration and site access. All attendees must comply with Brookhaven National Laboratory's REAL ID requirements for site access. Additional information is available at: https://www.bnl.gov/real-id/index.php. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to jfamiglie@bnl.gov no later than the date and time identified above and in accordance with the instructions contained in the solicitation. description: August 25, 2026: See attachment for a complete list of RFIs received to date. Some have already been answered, and the government is working to answer the rest. The government will continue to evaluate the need to extend the proposal deadline based on the time required to answer all questions and supply those answers to industry.
